concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: Section 8.1 of the original DPA required notice no later than 48 hours after awareness, and Amendment No. 1 (effective 1 October 2026) had not yet changed this on 15 September 2026.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1, Section A2.1, replaced Section 8.1 with a 24-hour outer limit, effective 1 October 2026 and in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1, Section A3.1, reduced the on-site audit notice period under Section 10.2 from 30 days to 20 days, effective 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: Amendment No. 1, Section A6.1, replaced Section 13.1 with a Processor aggregate liability cap of EUR 1,000,000, which applies from 1 October 2026 and is in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: Amendment No. 1, Section A6.1, states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap shall not apply to breaches of Section 4 (Confidentiality), so the cap does not cover confidentiality breaches.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed in Annex 3 as an approved Sub-processor, and its approval was only withdrawn with effect from 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: Amendment No. 1, Section A4.1, withdrew Meridian Mail Ltd's approval with effect from 1 January 2027, and the later emergency permission is limited to incident IR-27 from 9 to 11 May 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, processing and authorisation are established for Norway (existing storage), Estonia (Skylark Hosting), Lithuania (Baltika Analytics), France (Cendrillon Mail) and Denmark (Dagmar Backup), while Ireland is excluded because Meridian's approval was withdrawn on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: Under Section 12.1 as amended by Section A5.1 (60 days, effective 1 October 2026), 60 calendar days after 31 December 2026 is 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting personal data processed under the dpa.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting personal data processed under the DPA.
justifications: Amended Section 8.1 sets a 24-hour outer limit that replaces the original 48 hours and applies from 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The breach was confirmed to expose usable privileged credentials, so the 12-hour expedited outer limit applies from the original awareness, not the standard 24-hour limit. Later confirmation of the credential exposure does not change this.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness occurred at 17:10 on 9 April 2027, so the expedited 12-hour outer limit expired at 05:10 on 10 April. The first notice was delivered at 06:00 on 10 April, 50 minutes late.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: Counting from awareness on Friday 9 April, 12 April is a closure date and 14 April was the only approved pause day, so the third Business Day is 16 April. The refused 16 April pause does not extend the deadline.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The later hold, H-23, ends 25 August 2027, so release occurs then. Held records must be deleted by the later of the ordinary deadline (60 days after the 30 June 2027 termination, i.e. 29 August) and the tenth Business Day after release, which is 8 September 2027.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: BK-0630 was created on 30 June 2027 and contains no held records, so it must be deleted within 35 calendar days of creation. This is earlier than its ordinary deletion deadline of 29 August 2027, and restoring it does not restart the period.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: Records retained under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation, not service delivery or analytics. The analytics request for the held ORD records was rejected, and no other use is authorised.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Authorisation for the Stockholm infrastructure service requires the latest of the proposed start date, security review completion, and written Controller consent. The security review completed on 22 April, which is later than the 20 April start date and the 18 April consent, and actual processing began that day.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS was added as an approved Sub-processor for transactional email delivery from 1 January 2027 and continues that service. Meridian Mail Ltd's approval was withdrawn, and its emergency permission expired on 11 May 2027 and does not cover ordinary customer email.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: These countries have both actual processing and effective authorisation as of 15 May 2027, including data storage in Norway and Estonia, monitoring from Lithuania, email from France, and Stockholm infrastructure in Sweden. Ireland and Denmark lack effective authorisation on the queried date, and Finland and Germany have no authorised processing.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees of EUR 1,140,000 (EUR 1,440,000 incl. VAT less VAT and the EUR 60,000 credit) are doubled to EUR 2,280,000, which exceeds the EUR 2,000,000 minimum.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The EUR 1,000,000 ordinary cap per Contract Year less the EUR 300,000 already paid for ordinary breaches in this Contract Year leaves EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: Ordinary loss is capped at the remaining EUR 700,000, the security loss of EUR 1,750,000 fits within the remaining security cap of EUR 1,780,000, and the confidentiality-precedence losses of EUR 250,000 and EUR 100,000 are uncapped, totalling EUR 2,800,000.
